To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) the prevalence of HBV markers is very high among patients not vaccinated against HBV; 2) the prevalence of HCV antibodies is also high and 3) the risk for HIV is low.

the prevalence of HIV infection among dialysis patients in Italy is very low, that the rate of HBV infection is high among patients who have not received hepatitis B vaccine, and that the rate of HCV infection is very high among dialysis patients, especially those who have been on dialysis for more than 2 years.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a population of patients at risk for bloodborne infections.
the epidemiology of bloodborne infections among dialysis patients, and with the potential risks for staff who care of them.
the prevalence of HBV, HCV and HIV infections in Italian dialysis units, with particular reference to their possible transmission to staff.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prevalence of blood-borne infections among dialysis patients is still a matter for concern.
the prevalence of HIV, HBsAg, HBeAg and anti-HCV in dialysis units is low, but not negligible.
the prevalence of HIV, HBsAg, anti-HCV and anti-HIV in dialysis patients was 0.22, 9.2, 23 and 0.22%, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the prevalence of HIV, HBsAg and anti-HCV among dialysis patients is low, but not negligible; the prevalence of HBV markers is high among non-vaccinated patients, but low among vaccinated patients; the risk of HBV transmission from patients to staff is low among vaccinated patients and higher among non-vaccinates.
the risk of HBV and, especially, of HCV infection in dialysis patients is high, but the risk of HIV infection is very low.
the prevalence of bloodborne infections among Italian patients on maintenance dialysis is high, but the potential risk for healthcare workers is limited.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk of acquiring HIV, HBV or HCV infections from dialysis patients is not negligible.
dialysis units must be considered high-risk environments for the transmission of bloodborne infections and that the spread of these infections is still an important problem in Italy.
, in the absence of a vaccine, the best way to prevent the spread of bloodborne viruses is to prevent their introduction into the unit.
